name: Gement polder Netherlands 1140 AM 250212_0994
description: Polder ambience on winter-day on the Western outskirts of the city of 's-Hertogenbosch in the Netherlands. In the background the hum of the city.  Recorded close to bushes and trees.   Birds detected by Merlin Bird ID and me; Eurasian Coot, Eurasian Magpie, Eurasian Blu Tit, Greater White-fronted Goose, Great Tit, Carrion Crow, Eurasian Wren, European Robin Long-tailed Tit and Black-headed Gull (Eurasian Green Woodpecker visual) All tracks here today / More recording in Vughtse Gement polder About the area This polder is part of the Natura 2000 areas. A European network of protected natural areas. In these Natura 2000 areas, certain animals, plants and their natural habitats are protected to preserve biodiversity (species diversity). In Vlijmens Ven, the area where we are now, very well-developed ditch vegetation occurs here. These include wreath weed communities, Water Soldiers and Pondweed vegetation and Bank weed vegetation. The occurrence of these vegetations is mainly due to the strong inflow of seepage water. Underground seepage water flows from the sand ridge on which the Vughtse Heide and the Loonse and Drunense Dunes lie. This water of good quality . The larva of this species first feeds on Sanguisorba officinalis (great burnet), then moves onto ant nests and is a predator of the ant brood. Myrmica rubra and Myrmica scabrinodis have been reported as frequent host ant species. The rare Bewick's Swan can be seen in this area from late September to late March. They winter mainly on grasslands and fields. These swans breed on the arctic tundra along the Barents Sea and further east. The population has declined in recent years. Raptors like Buzzard, Eurasian Hobby and Eurasian Sparrowhawk thrive in the inaccessible swamp forests of the adjacent Marshes and partly seek their food in surrounding fields and the adjoining city. Woodpeckers, including Lesser Spotted Woodpecker and Eurasian Green Woodpecker, breed in the older parts. This is also an ideal area for many songbirds and nest in the marshy parts. The Canada goose has settled in. It is now a little too successful because it has established itself in the western residential areas of the city with 500 pieces and is causing a lot of poop nuisance there. Kingfisher, Great Yellow Wagtail and Great Egret are here during migration and in winter. In winter, the surrounding fields are an important foraging area for (thousands of) geese and swans. Particularly Greylag Goose, Reed Goose (both Taiga and Tundra Goose), Lesser Swan, Wild Swan and sometimes Barnacle Goose and Red-necked Goose are observed during this time. name: floodplain river Maas close to village Hedikhuizen Netherlands 1140 am 260303_0081
description:
Atmosphere of the Meuse floodplains near Hedikhuizen on a windless spring day in March. At the foot of the winter dyke, in the floodplain of the Meuse near Hedikhuizen in the Netherlands, about 50 metres from the water, on a windless day in March like today, you can hear the birds, the traffic on the other side of the river, shipping.
About the picture A wide, open riverside landscape stretches out under a clear, pale‑blue sky. It is early afternoon in March, and the light is soft but bright. In the foreground lies the flat floodplain, divided here and there by simple wooden fences. The grass is short and fresh. A little farther away, a broad river Maas flows gently through the scene. Along its near bank stand patches of tall, dry reeds in light brown tones. On the water, a large cargo boat moves steadily from left to right, creating the only sense of motion in an otherwise quiet setting. Beyond the river, the land rises slightly into the floodplain. A line of trees borders the water; some are bare, still waiting for their leaves after winter, while others show the first signs of budding.

About the floodplain The floodplain near Hedikhuizen is an ecologically valuable area along the Meuse River, with a rich history and an important role in water management and nature development. The floodplains are the low-lying lands between the river and the winter dyke. At Hedikhuizen, they form a characteristic part of the Meuse landscape, with a mix of nature, cultural history and hydrological functions. The floodplain consists of grasslands, reed beds and marshy areas. This variety provides habitat for numerous species, including water birds, amphibians and insects. Here you will find species such as the yellow wagtail, reed warbler, and sometimes even the beaver. The flora includes marsh plants such as cattail, meadowsweet, and marsh marigold. Due to its relative tranquillity and limited development, the area is attractive to breeding birds and wintering waterfowl. The dyke and floodplain are accessible via various footpaths. Cyclists can cycle for miles along the dykes, which are closed to motor vehicles.

name: Dutch polder Gelderse Waarden Noord-Brabant Netherlands  226 pm 250320_1061
description: Polder Farmland Netherlands early spring with many birds. In the background, the low tones, or more the hum of distant cars and tractor. Here in the Gelderse Waarden, a vast polder near Hedikhuizen, peace prevails. The chiffchaff and the green woodpecker, the stock dove and the crow, and many other birds make themselves heard. The airplanes and the man on the bicycle are free extras in this recording. He’s calling and waving at me. Occasionally, some traffic passes through the polder. A farmer drives his tractor. Other than that, not much happens. It’s wonderfully quiet here. Birds detected by Merlin Bird ID app (ver. 3.7.2 (256 – 2025) #0:10 Common Magpie #0:08 #0:10 #0:13 #0:43 #0:50 Long-tailed Tit #0:57 Common Pheasant #0:05 #0:11 #0:18 #0:30 #0:44 #0:54 Common Chiffchaff #0:38 #0:52 Eurasian Wren #0:01 Stoke dove #0:01 Common Kingfisher (beeps) About the location To my left and in front of me lies the Hoge Maasdijk (a river-dike), which protects the 'Gelderse Waarden' (left, the polder) from high water levels of the River Maas. The Gelderse Waarden is a peculiar name, as this polder does not belong to the province of Gelderland but to Noord-Brabant. Here’s the backstory: Once, the Hedikhuizense Maas flowed through this area—a sharp meander of the River Maas that was cut through in 1474-1475 to facilitate shipping. The area north of this meander, which is now south of the river Maas, remained part of Gelderland as the Gelderse Waarden until 1958. From that point onward, this polder became part of the province of Noord-Brabant. name: calm down-town street noise s-Hertogenbosch Netherlands  10 am 251210_0057
description:
Ambient calm down-town street noise. A driver rolls a pallet out of the lorry. Then an electrically operated metal gate opens and closes again. Is that high-pitched squeak coming from a dunnock or a kingfisher?
The photo you shared shows an atmospheric part of the Verwerstroom, a characteristic section of the Binnendieze river in the heart of 's-Hertogenbosch. A narrow, tranquil waterway winds its way between historic brick buildings. The calm stream reflects the facades and the sky above like a mirror. Ivy and other rare greenery grow along and on the walls, contrasting beautifully with the robust restored brickwork. A wooden bridge with black classic metal railings spans the Verwerstroom. On the right-hand side of the bridge is an electrically operated gate. In the background, a mix of architectural styles: from classic red roof tiles to a modern glass building. This combination emphasises how 's-Hertogenbosch harmoniously interweaves its rich past with contemporary elements.

About the recording setting Echo of urban sounds that are audible beneath the vaults of the overpass above the water. A microphone hangs above the water of the 'Verwersstroom', a part of the city-river Binnendieze, in the old Dutch city of 's-Hertogenbosch. This sound recording captures the subtle echoes of city life reverberating beneath the arched bridge vault above the water. Together, the image and sound evoke a layered sensory experience of 's-Hertogenbosch, where history, architecture, and ambient sounds converge in a quiet moment of urban beauty.
About The Binnendieze / Verwerstroom. A Hidden Waterway Through History: Flowing quietly through the heart of ’s-Hertogenbosch, the Binnendieze is more than just a canal—it’s a living monument to the city’s medieval past. This intricate network of narrow waterways once served as a vital system for defense, drainage, and transport within the city walls. This part of De Binnendieze is called De Verwersstroom. Over centuries, buildings and streets were constructed above it, creating a unique underground river that winds beneath homes, courtyards, and alleyways. Today, the Binnendieze offers a rare glimpse into the layered history of the city. Restored with care in the late 20th century, it now welcomes visitors on guided boat tours, gliding beneath centuries-old arches and alongside moss-covered walls. As you drift through hidden passages and open stretches, the blend of architecture and nature reveals how ’s-Hertogenbosch has embraced its heritage while preserving its charm. Here, the water flows beneath the square in front of the Government Building (now the Noord-Brabants Museum) and is approximately 3.2 meters wide at that point. The newly constructed brick archway is 44.25 meters long and dates back to the time of the Government Building’s construction. More information about De Binnendieze

name: Tropical Orchard in Spring
description: The official name of this place is Chintamoni Kar Bird Sanctuary. Located near Calcutta, it is essentially a bird rich orchard with large mango and other trees. The sound scape was recorded at around quarter past six in the morning. The birds heard here are black-hooded oriole, Asian Koel, rose-ringed parakeet, white-browed fantail, coppersmith barbet, common mynah, oriental magpie robin, jungle babbler, spotted dove, rufous treepie, white-breasted kingfisher,
